claim.pdf_says: [Table A.1 continued from p1047 - the table on this page begins directly with a DATA row, with no repeated column-header row:] | START | any | no | no |  then  | WRITE | Automatic - single | no | - on any previously locked record | ...
claim.markdown_says:
| START | any | no | no |
|-------|-----|----|----|
| WRITE | Automatic - single | no | - on any previously locked record |
| | - multiple | no | no |
claim.why_it_matters: The markdown places the GFM header separator (|---|---|---|---|) immediately after the START row, which makes 'START / any / no / no' render as the table's column-heading row. The continuation table then has no column names at all, and the START row - a data row of Table A.1 stating that the START statement sets no lock and releases none - is presented as a label. A reader of the rendered markdown cannot tell which column is 'Lock is set' and which is 'Lock for same logical file is released', so the WRITE and UNLOCK rows below it lose their column semantics.

verdict.reasoning:
REFUTED. I rendered both p1048 and p1047 at 300 dpi and read the transcription for both pages.

(1) The claim's factual premise about the two sources is correct as far as it goes: PDF p1048 (printed folio 1018) does begin Table A.1's continuation directly with a data row - I can see 'START | any | no | no' drawn in the same plain roman face as the WRITE and UNLOCK rows below it, with no bold header row and no repeated 'I-O statement / Lock mode / Lock is set / Lock for same logical file is released' band (that band appears only on p1047, where it is set in bold above a heavier rule). And specs/ISO_COBOL.md p1048 lines 10-11 do read '| START | any | no | no |' followed by '|-------|-----|----|----|'.

(2) But no spec CONTENT differs. Every cell of the START row is present, in the correct order, in the correct four columns, at the correct position (first row of the continuation). Nothing is missing, added, reordered, or altered. The entire complaint is the placement of a GFM separator line, which is a pure markdown-format artifact: GFM has no syntax for a headerless table, so a table split at a page boundary in a page-per-section transcription must promote its first line to a header. That is page-break furniture and formatting - explicitly the disqualifying category.

(3) The claim's stated harm is causally wrong. It asserts the separator placement is why 'the continuation table then has no column names at all' and why a reader 'cannot tell which column is Lock is set'. The column names are absent from the SOURCE page: ISO itself did not repeat the header band on p1048. A perfectly faithful transcription of p1048 in isolation would also have no column names, and a reader of PDF p1048 alone must likewise flip back to p1047 to recover them. The markdown loses nothing the PDF page does not also lack.

(4) The residual delta is cosmetic and confined to rendering: a viewer of the rendered markdown sees START/any/no/no emboldened and centered as a heading rather than as a plain data row. The four cells still read correctly against p1047's column order. No semantic, syntactic, or normative content of Table A.1 is changed, and no rule about the START statement's lock behaviour is lost or misstated - the row still says START sets no lock and releases none.

The transcription is otherwise faithful on this page: it correctly repeats the 'Table A.1 Summary of record lock acquisition and release' title and the 'For files subject to commit and rollback...' lead paragraph that the PDF also repeats on p1048, preserves the empty 'Lock is set' cell on the UNLOCK row, and carries D.2.4.4 Retry and D.2.5 Commit and rollback verbatim.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a content discrepancy. The claim accurately describes both sources but misattributes the effect. All of Table A.1's p1048 content is transcribed correctly and completely; the only difference is that the GFM header separator sits after the first data row, which is unavoidable because GFM cannot express a headerless table and this table is split across a page boundary. The absence of column names on the continuation is a property of the ISO page itself (ISO does not repeat the header band on p1048), not of the transcription. If anything is worth doing, it is a cosmetic, whole-document improvement to the page-split table convention - e.g. re-emitting the p1047 header row ('| I-O statement | Lock mode | Lock is set | Lock for same logical file is released |') at the top of every continuation table, or annotating the continuation as '(Table A.1 continued)' - filed as a transcription-style nit, not a structural spec-fidelity defect.
